title: [D2 Context] Completeness, context versioning and the retention boundary
summary: sql/migrations/0009_retention_boundary.sql puts a retention boundary around the context views — two retained materialized views under one 24-hour temporal filter, a live plain view carrying `completeness` (`open`/`provisional`, no `final`) and a `context_version` digest, a rejection counter over the unbounded aggregate, and `helena_frozen_context`, the copy-out table. helena.context gains its first Python: ContextStore.freeze (copy a cited context out before it is evicted, typed refusal when it is already gone), ContextStore.frozen, and ContextStore.rejections with a rate that refuses to be 0.0 over no records.
assumption_validated: Four things, all measured against RisingWave 3.0.3 before the migration was written and all now tests. (1) A temporal filter in a materialized view over the context aggregate is accepted and REALLY EVICTS: a context 277.6 s past its window, under a 283-second horizon, was present at creation and gone 5 s after the horizon passed, while the aggregate behind it kept the row. So engine-side retention as a temporal filter is available as concept/06 costs it (~1.9 bytes/record), not merely as a read-time predicate. (2) A LATE RECORD INSIDE THE BOUNDARY STILL REVISES UNDER A TEMPORAL FILTER — concept/08-open-questions.md had this as untested and not to be inferred; it is now measured (1 flow / 77 octets became 2 / 1380 through the filter, context_id unchanged) and the note has been updated to say so. (3) `now()` is refused everywhere but WHERE/HAVING/ON/FROM in a streaming query, so `completeness` CANNOT be a materialized column — that constraint, not a preference, is why the citable row is a plain view. (4) A batch query over a plain view evaluates now() per read, so completeness is a property of when the row was read.
makes_buildable: The enriched-context view (D3, task 24) now has a bounded, citable object to build on — helena_signal_host_context_live, with its entity rows in helena_signal_context_entities_retained — instead of an aggregate that grows without limit. The finding/citation increment (D4/D5) has the copy-out it needs: ContextStore.freeze plus the (context_id, context_version) pair a citation records, and the typed ContextOutsideRetention that says a citation came too late. The rejection counter is the instrument concept/08 says the horizon itself must be chosen with.

verification.detail: 572 passed in 2142.56s (0:35:42), full suite, against a throwaway in-memory ./bin/risingwave single_node. Every SQL claim is executed: the six new objects are read back out of information_schema and rw_catalog, the boundary is exercised over real records (the 2024 fixtures outside it, real records with a re-stamped `ts` inside it), and the eviction test waits out a computed short horizon on a probe view and watches the row leave. Mutation-checked: making the completeness CASE return 'provisional' in both branches fails test_completeness_is_open_while_the_window_is_and_provisional_after, and dropping bytes_received from the version digest fails test_the_context_version_is_a_digest_of_the_id_and_the_statistics; the migration was restored byte-identically (md5 verified) and the affected tests re-run green.

escalations.detail: The retention horizon is 24 hours in the code and it is a CANDIDATE, not a decision. concept/08-open-questions.md records the horizon as unset and to be chosen by watching the rejection counter, so a value had to exist for the boundary to be built at all. It is labelled as a candidate in the migration head, in helena.context.RETENTION_HORIZON's comment, in the README and in concept/08, and changing it is a new migration. The operator may want to set it deliberately once real traffic has been through helena_signal_retention_rejections.

The task says 'one configured horizon'. It is NOT an environment variable, deliberately: a streaming temporal filter takes a literal, so an env var would be a value the running view ignores — the silent-configuration-default trap in instruction.md §6, wearing the opposite mask. It is a project constant with an engine-side copy, changed by a migration, with all three homes asserted equal by execution. If the operator wants deployment-time configuration of the horizon, that is a decision about generating or parameterising migrations and it is not made here.

invariant_conflicts.step: Add a test that a revised context produces a new version rather than editing in place
invariant_conflicts.conflict: As written this contradicts concept/07-principles.md as it now stands. The note was corrected on 2026-09-04 — 'A revised context keeps its identity: the counters change in place and the context_id does not' — after task 13 measured that an incrementally maintained view edits in place, and concept/08 settles the same thing. Authority order puts concept/ above the task, so the step was not implemented as written.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: The compatible half was implemented and is what the tests assert: identity stable, VERSION new. `context_version` is a digest of the context id and its six statistics, so a revision leaves context_id alone and mints a new version — 'a revised context is a new version rather than an edit in place' is true of the thing a citation records, which is the property the step was after. test_a_revised_context_mints_a_new_version_and_keeps_its_identity asserts both halves, and test_a_frozen_context_survives_the_revision_of_the_context_it_copied shows what it buys: the copy taken before the revision still says what the citation was issued against.

invariant_conflicts.step: Record as untested and not to be inferred whether a late record inside the boundary still revises under a temporal filter
invariant_conflicts.conflict: instruction.md §4 forbids inferring a behaviour that can be tested, and this one can be tested. Recording it as untested when the repository can measure it would have left a note that is wrong.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Measured instead, and the concept note updated to record the measurement, the test that holds it, and what is still NOT covered — a record arriving for a window that has just left the horizon, which is a boundary crossing this fixture set cannot construct without waiting out a real horizon.

deferred: Freezing entity rows. helena_signal_context_entities_retained is bounded (it joins the retained context, so an entity row cannot outlive its context) but there is no frozen copy of one. What a finding cites is decided by the finding contract, and there is no finding contract yet (D4/D5) — inventing the shape now would be the speculative abstraction instruction.md §1 forbids. Recorded as deferred in the migration head and the module docstring.

A caller for freeze(). Nothing cites a context yet, so nothing is copied out yet. What is demonstrated is that a frozen copy survives a revision of the context it copied — NOT that a copy is taken at the right moment, which needs the code that issues a finding.

Exposing the rejection counter through helena.observability. It is exposed the way every other counter in this project is — a queryable view plus a typed reader (ContextStore.rejections) that reconciles its own numbers, the same idiom as helena_ingest_counts and helena_ingest_quarantine_counts. No pipeline stage logs anything yet, so wiring one metric into the log channel would be a stage that does not exist.
Deliberate choice of the horizon. See the escalation.
lessons: task 16: RisingWave 3.0.3 accepts a temporal filter in a materialized view over an UPDATABLE materialized view (the context aggregate), and the filter really evicts — measured: window_end 277.6 s old, horizon 283 s, row present at creation, gone 5 s after the horizon passed, the aggregate behind it unchanged. So retention as concept/06 costs it is available, and 'retention is a filter, not a delete' is literally true of the row behind the filter.

task 16: A late record inside the boundary STILL REVISES through a temporal filter — concept/08 had it as untested and not to be inferred; the retained row went 1 flow / 77 octets to 2 / 1380 with the context_id unchanged, exactly like the aggregate. The note now records the measurement.

task 16: `now()` is REFUSED outside WHERE / HAVING / ON / FROM in a RisingWave streaming query — `CASE WHEN window_end > now() THEN ... END` in the select list of a materialized view fails to bind with a message naming the four allowed clauses. Any column that is a function of the clock therefore has to live on a plain view and be evaluated per read. That is what forced the retained-view / live-view split, and it is worth knowing before anyone tries to materialize a staleness or age column.

task 16: `rw_catalog.rw_materialized_views` (and `rw_views`) hold the definition the engine received, normalized and comment-free, and they carry `schema_name` — SCOPE THE QUERY BY `schema_name = current_schema()`, because the catalogue is cluster-wide and every per-test schema holds a same-named view. This is the way to assert an SQL literal equals a Python constant exactly: pull `INTERVAL '...'` out of the stored definition and hand it back to the engine to evaluate. Grepping the .sql file would find the value in the comment that explains it.

task 16: Every fixture in this repository is dated 2024-06-01, so any retention horizon a prototype would set puts ALL of them outside the boundary. A test of anything clock-relative has to re-stamp `ts` on a real record (task 12's technique) — and the 2024 fixtures then become a free, real 'outside the boundary' case, which is how the rejection counter gets a numerator that is not made up.

task 16: `count(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)` and `sum(x) FILTER (WHERE ...)` work in a RisingWave batch (plain) view, including with `now()` in the filter, and an INTERVAL column reaches psycopg as a timedelta. `INSERT ... SELECT` into a table also works, needs a FLUSH before the rows are readable, and reports rowcount — but it cannot tell the caller WHICH row it wrote, which is why freeze() reads then writes.

task 16: Two identities on one row pull the settled argument apart cleanly: `context_id` says which host in which window under which aggregation (stable across revisions, by measurement), `context_version` says which numbers (new on every revision). A citation records both. This is what makes concept/07's 'a citation must be stable, not merely current' implementable without contradicting concept/07's own correction that identity is stable across revisions.
failed_approaches: task 16: Putting `completeness` on the retained materialized view. Written and rejected by the engine, not by taste: `now()` outside WHERE is refused in a streaming query. The retained view / live view split exists because of that measurement.

task 16: A `CROSS JOIN helena_retention_horizon` inside the retained materialized view, so the horizon would have one home. Not attempted against the engine because 0002 already measured the refusal ('Not supported: streaming nested-loop join') for exactly this shape with the aggregation version. The horizon therefore has two homes in SQL and the catalogue comparison is what keeps them equal.

task 16: Repeating the temporal predicate on the entity rows' own `window_end` to bound them. Rejected before it was written for the reason task 14 recorded about the window interval: a second copy of the constant is a second thing to bump, and a drifted copy produces plausible wrong rows. The retained entity view joins the retained context instead, so an entity row is inside the boundary exactly when its context is, by construction.

task 16: Making the rejection counter read the retained view. It could only ever report zero — the rows it has to count are the ones that view exists to remove. It reads the unbounded aggregate, and that is the one place in the layer that does.

task 16: Letting ContextStore.rejections() fall back to the Python RETENTION_HORIZON constant when the counter has no rows (no contexts yet). It would make an empty counter agree with this process about a store some other migration built; it reads helena_retention_horizon instead, and raises if even that is empty.

task 16: A `frozen_at` timestamp on the frozen row. Rejected for the reason task 09 rejected `quarantined_at`: every other column is derived from the context, so freezing twice is a byte-identical upsert and replay reproduces it — a timestamp would make the row a fact about a run and, under the upsert, would silently come to mean 'the last time this was frozen'. When a finding exists, when it was issued is a property of the finding.

task 16: `SELECT definition FROM rw_catalog.rw_materialized_views WHERE name = ...` without a schema predicate. It returns one row per schema holding a same-named view, so it fails as soon as a second test schema (or a leftover probe schema) exists on the same engine.
next_session_should_know: The signal layer now has a boundary above it, and the next thing built on a context should read helena_signal_host_context_live (bounded, plus completeness and context_version) rather than helena_signal_host_context — the unbounded aggregate is now only for the rejection counter and for replay of archived captures. Two practical consequences. FIRST: over every fixture in this repository the retained views are EMPTY, because the fixtures are dated 2024-06-01 and the horizon is 24 hours; a test that needs a live context must re-stamp `ts` on a real record (tests/test_context.py::restamped and ::current_window are there for it), and a test that queries a retained view over the plain layer capture will correctly see nothing. SECOND: helena.context is no longer SQL-only — ContextStore is the writer for helena_frozen_context and the reader for the rejection counter, and the module docstring's table lists what each migration contributes. The horizon is a candidate at 24 hours, not a decision; if a session wants to change it, that is a new migration that drops and recreates all four views and the table, and helena.context.RETENTION_HORIZON has to move with it — the suite asserts the three copies equal by asking the engine, including the interval RisingWave stored in the retained view's own definition, so a partial change fails loudly. Task 17 is the view-layering boundary tests and materialization policy: the objects added here declare themselves in tests/test_context.py::test_every_signal_object_declares_what_it_is (prefix query over helena_signal_%) and ::test_the_retention_objects_declare_what_they_are, and the two retained views are the first materialized views in the layer whose reason to be materialized is state eviction rather than being a join target — worth saying explicitly in whatever policy that task writes down.
